Herein, we develop a machine-learning framework for predicting phase stability using a carefully curated RHEA dataset that combines secondary phase-inspired descriptors, refined synthesis metadata, and reassessed phase labels. The resulting ML model achieves a high predictive performance (F1 score = 0.89) in identifying single-phase solid solution RHEAs.

abstractExcerpt: Principal component analysis (PCA) is widely used to characterize collective protein motions from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. While PCA identifies the dominant modes of structural fluctuation, it does not reveal whether different principal components (PCs) causally influence each other. Here, we investigate this question using a recently introduced causal-discovery framework [Del Tatto et al, PNAS 2024], which allows to infer putative causal asymmetries between high-dimensional time series. We apply this approach to long-timescale MD trajectories of two proteins.

title: Inverse Designing Reconfigurable Piezoelectric Tensors via Architectural and Modal Programming
abstractExcerpt: Piezoelectricity arises from the coupling between electric polarization and mechanical deformation, described by a third-rank tensor whose coefficients are constrained by crystal symmetry. In natural crystals, atomic periodicity and energetic stability restrict accessible symmetries, limited to 20 distinct anisotropies that can exist. Here we establish a general framework, based on graph representation, for controlling the full effective piezoelectric tensor through architecture by resolving how macroscopic symmetry, local polarization and deformation of structural elements act together.

abstractExcerpt: We investigate the Jahn-Teller structural phase transition in LaMnO3 at TJT ≃ 750 K using molecular dynamics simulations based on machine-learning force fields trained on ab initio data.
